programs.title: Blue Planet 2: The Making of
programs.desc: Behind the scenes of the creation of a spectacular nature series that took 4 years to film.The teams implementing it visited all oceans.Thanks to the fact that the divers had the latest equipment, they could have very close encounters with the animals being filmed.Even in low light conditions, the cameras captured events invisible to the human eye.Inspection cameras show the lives of small creatures, and those equipped with a suction cup record what is happening in the ocean from the perspective of larger animals.Wanting to film the most extraordinary wildlife scenes, the team also visited coastlines in the farthest corners of the world, such as the Galapagos Islands.Marine life around these islands depends on cold currents feeding surface waters.

programs.title: Where the Wild Men Are with Ben Fogle
programs.desc: Famous adventurer Ben Fogle interviews and meets people who have made a risky decision, leaving their life in Western society and settling in the middle of nowhere, far from civilization.

programs.title: Life Below Zero: Canada
programs.desc: The creators of the series present the everyday life of a group of daredevils struggling with wildlife in various regions of northern Canada during a frosty winter.Johnatan Granier will join the program in the second season.

programs.title: The World's Deadliest Weather
programs.desc: Moving accounts of people who survived confrontations with the forces of nature.This series includes, among others:memories of earthquakes in Turkey and Syria and fires raging in Los Angeles.

programs.title: The Boxing Day Tsunami
programs.desc: On December 26, 2004, the second day of Christmas, a devastating tsunami hit Indonesia and Thailand.It was the largest disaster of this type in history, and its dramatic effects were also felt in other parts of the world.It started with an earthquake under the Indian Ocean.A few minutes later, a hundred-meter wall of water broke through Indonesia.Then the tsunami reached Thailand, where it left unimaginable destruction in its wake.Scientists analyze the course of these tragic events and explain the connection between the earthquake and the subsequent tsunami.Rescuers give accounts of the fierce fight to save human lives, and survivors recall their losses in a tragedy that is difficult to recover from even after many years.
